recognition: Recognized by Russia and a small number of other states. The EU rejects the legality of its separate presidential elections.
provenance: Researched dossier. Each cited source has its own date; the newest citation is not a live verification of every field. No control geometry is inferred from areas of activity.

name: South Ossetia / Tskhinvali region
summary: Breakaway polity within Georgia’s internationally recognized borders. Its de facto institutions and security remain closely tied to Russia.
currency: Russian ruble (documented in the 2010 institutional study; a current currency review is pending).
economy: Historically highly dependent on Russian financial assistance; current economic measures are not verified here.
military: De facto security structures and Russian forces; no current deployment map is supplied.
origin: Armed conflict during the Soviet collapse led to a 1992 ceasefire; the 2008 war deepened separation from Georgia.
startBasis: 1992 marks the ceasefire consolidating de facto separation; earlier declarations and later Russian recognition are separate events.
